instrument: Perpres 10/2021 as amended by 49/2021, Lampiran II
population: SPLIT HEIRS — annex rows whose 2020 code fans out to several 2025 codes. The prior spec (umkm_lampiran_ii_readjudicated_2026_08_06.json) deliberately excluded every one of these, because a 1:1 crosswalk edge was its only mechanical proof of identity and a split has none.
adjudicated: 2026-08-06, generator!=grader and cross-family: a Claude Sonnet 5 lane proposes one verdict per candidate 2025 code, a Codex GPT-5.6 lane re-derives blind on fresh context without seeing the proposal. Only codes where BOTH lanes independently returned PATCH_ZERO are here. 62 candidate 2025 codes across 12 annex rows were judged; four survived.
decisive_test: The REVERSE direction. Forward ('did the 2020 activity split?') cannot name the heir. Reverse ('does this 2025 code absorb any OTHER 2020 code?') can: an heir that absorbs nothing else cannot be wider than the row the annex reserves. All four absorb exactly one ancestor, and it is the annex's.
parent_headings: None of these four rows sits under a qualifier-carrying parent heading. For 'Hotel Bintang I' the governing heading is 'Jasa Penginapan', read here from the annex as regenerated by the dotted-item fix (#3667) rather than from the copy this branch started on; it names a service class, carries no size/technology/scope qualifier and narrows nothing. The other three rows have no parent heading at all.

objection_raised_and_answered.objection: A cross-family review of the finished determination (Codex GPT-5.6, instructed to refute, verdict DEFECTIVE) called `96100` a BLOCKER: the annex row says only 'Penatu', while the 2025 code's own uraian enumerates dry-cleaning, fur and textiles, carpets and rugs, curtains, combined rental-and-care, and reusable-diaper services. On that reading the reservation would be narrower than the code being closed, and a PMA dry-cleaning or carpet-cleaning business would be told 0% without proof.
objection_raised_and_answered.answer: Two things the objection did not weigh. (1) The annex row's code column is the 2020 code `96200`, whose own BPS title is 'Aktivitas penatu' — so the row names the WHOLE 2020 code by its own name, not a slice of it, and Pasal 5(5) then attaches the allocation to that whole bidang usaha. (2) If the 2025 code had gained scope from somewhere else in the recatalogue, BPS's crosswalk would name that somewhere else as an ancestor; it names exactly one, `96200`. The enumerated services are the ISIC-9601 explanatory text that the class carries in both vintages, not new territory. The same objection, if it stood, would equally condemn `96210` — which covers colouring, perming and straightening, arguably beyond 'barber shop' — and `96220`, which covers nail art, eyelash extensions and tanning, arguably beyond 'salon kecantikan'. It was raised against `96100` because that code's uraian is the most enumerative of the three, not because its evidence is weaker.
objection_raised_and_answered.what_this_rests_on_and_does_not_prove: A SECOND review (GLM 5.2, a third family) refuted the limit this field originally named, and it was right. The first version said the reasoning 'rests on BPS's crosswalk being complete' — a narrower limit that hides the real one. The crosswalk records MERGES: a 2025 code that absorbed several 2020 codes. It does not record DESCRIPTION REWRITES, and BPS can widen a code's scope without merging anything from anywhere, which no ancestor edge could capture even in a perfect crosswalk. There is visible evidence of rewriting here: 2020 'Aktivitas penatu' became 2025 'Aktivitas Pencucian dan Pembersihan Produk Tekstil dan Bulu', broader in plain language. So the honest limit is: the 2025 scope can exceed the 2020 scope with no edge to show it; we do not hold the KBLI-2020 catalogue text to rule that out; and the step 'annex label == BPS title == the code's whole scope' is circular exactly when the code's scope is what is in question. Load-bearing for the whole reverse-direction method, including the nine codes of #3666 — not special to these four. What the evidence DOES establish, and it is not nothing: no OTHER 2020 code feeds these heirs, so the heir did not swallow a second activity alongside the reserved one.
objection_raised_and_answered.a_field_that_looks_like_evidence_and_is_: The crosswalk edges carry `sebagian_2020` and `sebagian_2025` ('partial') flags, which would settle whole-versus-slice mechanically if they were populated. Measured across all 2,560 edges: True on ZERO of them, both fields. A field that is constant over the entire corpus carries no information, and it reads as a strong signal ('nothing is partial') precisely when it is none. Do not cite it.
objection_raised_and_answered.why_55105_stands_on_different_ground: For the other three the argument is 'the annex names the whole 2020 code'. For `55105` it cannot be: the annex text is 'Hotel Bintang I' while the 2020 title is 'Hotel Bintang', all grades — the row names something NARROWER than the code. The argument there is the other one, that the 2025 code IS exactly the named grade, which is also why 55101-55104 stay open. Note that the annex parser's `title_corroborated` flag reads True on that row, so it is a fuzzy match and cannot be used to tell 'names the whole code' from 'names a slice'.
objection_raised_and_answered.the_honesty_applied_unevenly: The 55105 entry states plainly that the annex row is NARROWER than the 2020 code and switches to a different argument. The same structure recurs for 96100/96210/96220 and the first draft did not say so: an annex row is a plain-language LABEL, not a scope definition, so 'the row names the whole 2020 code' is a reading of the label rather than a fact read off the instrument. Recorded so a future reader weighs these three at the strength they actually have, and does not cite this spec as if identity had been proven mechanically for them.
objection_raised_and_answered.corroboration_from_a_layer_that_judged_e: Not proof, and named as such — but 96210, 96220 and 96100 already carry l4_bali.status CHIUSO_PMA_NO_BESAR with blocked=true, confidence HIGH, each citing Lampiran II p.16 entry 57 and its own 2020 code. That determination was made by a different pass at a different time, and the live site has been publishing 'Reserved for MSME — closed to PT PMA' on those three while the national ceiling still read 100%. This cure makes the two halves agree. 55105 has no such corroboration: its l4_bali is an OSS-scope verdict (BLOCCATO_DIPENDE_SCOPE, blocked=false, MEDIUM) with nothing to do with Lampiran II.

retail_and_construction_rows_all_refused.outcome: every candidate refused as BROADER (one as SEGMENT). Nothing to patch.
retail_and_construction_rows_all_refused.note: In the orchestrated run the grader lane for these rows received the literal string 'undefined' as its evidence path — an unfilled variable in the workflow script — and REFUSED to reason from files it had not been given rather than inventing verdicts. They were re-derived afterwards against the real path; the verdicts recorded here are the re-derived ones.

the_one_segment_refusal_named.why: The annex reserves motorcycle repair only 'yang terintegrasi dengan bidang usaha penjualan sepeda motor' — integrated with the motorcycle-SALES business. 95320's own uraian is general motorcycle repair and maintenance with no such restriction, so it plainly also covers standalone workshops the annex never reserved. Pasal 5(5): the allocation attaches to the named (qualified) bidang usaha, not to the code number. Left open, and belongs to the grade/segment-qualified population whose deliverable is a page disclosure, not a cap flip.
the_one_segment_refusal_named.why_it_is_named_here: It was previously covered only by the aggregate 'every candidate refused as BROADER (one as SEGMENT)'. An unnamed member of a population cannot be picked up by the pass that closes it — the same reason the withdrawn spec names its eleven tainted codes one by one instead of saying 'thirty-nine, re-check them all'.
the_one_segment_refusal_named.corroborated_by: An independent peer session re-derived all seven verdicts for the 43305 and 45407 rows from the dataset; its absorption counts were re-checked here against bps_2020_ancestors and match exactly (43301 -> [43301,43304] besides the annex code, 43400 -> 29 others, 95400 -> 9 others, 95320 -> none).

retail_and_construction_rows_all_refused.a_row_whose_reserved_activity_we_cannot_: The 45407 annex row's text is ONLY a qualifier — 'yang terintegrasi dengan bidang usaha penjualan sepeda motor' — with no activity noun and no parent_heading captured. A row beginning with 'yang' is grammatically a continuation of a heading above it, so the heading was lost. Measured: exactly 1 such orphan in the annex's 181 rows, pinned by a test so a parser change that creates more is caught and a fix that resolves this one is noticed. It changes no verdict here (the row is refused either way, and a segment reservation is not expressible in a single cap anyway), but we are holding a reservation whose reserved activity we cannot state.

agreed_to_refuse_but_labelled_differentl.detail: one lane REFUSE_SEGMENT, the other REFUSE_UNCLEAR — same outcome (leave open), different name for why. No action either way.

bias_stated_to_both_lanes: A wrongly-restricted code costs a client a business they could lawfully run; that is not a safer error, it is a different error. REFUSE_UNCLEAR was a real option. Refusing is NOT the safe direction — the opposite error tells a client he may wholly own a reserved activity.
